topic: Measuring Voltage, Current, Resistance and Waveforms
title: Where Do the Probes Go? Explained Simply | PUC Electronics Class 11
description:
Aarav's bicycle lamp is glowing dim and he picks up a meter. But where do the probes go? In this animated lesson we measure the three quantities of every circuit on a live breadboard: voltage with a voltmeter across the part (in parallel), current with an ammeter in the path (in series), and resistance with an ohmmeter, only with the power off and the part on its own. You see why a good voltmeter has a very high resistance and a good ammeter a very low one.

Then the oscilloscope: the screen grid of divisions, the volts per division and time per division knobs, and a signal generator whose wave grows taller and crowds closer as you turn it up. We read any wave in small steps (Vpp, Vm, Vrms = Vm/root 2, period T and frequency f = 1/T), work out a full example (8 V peak to peak, 2.83 V rms, 50 Hz), and finish with the exam trap (an ammeter across a part), where it is asked, an original practice question with a full solution, and a formula card to screenshot.

This is Episode 22 of PUC Electronics, Class 11, Chapter 3: Measuring Instruments (Karnataka PUC Electronics).

In this video:
